brief.headline: Wall Street had its best day since April 2025 after Nvidia brought back Jensen Huang as chief executive

sections.text: Nvidia's board reinstated Huang less than two weeks after he resigned, and the relief lifted the whole AI trade: the Philadelphia semiconductor index (a basket of US chip companies) jumped 14% and the Dow gained 3.0% to 49,595.31. The S&P 500 ended a seven-day losing run and won back about half of last week's 8.6% fall, taking it out of correction territory: it is now about 7.4% below its October record. The VIX (the 'fear gauge') fell 26% to 26.62. In Europe the Stoxx 600 rose 1.8% to 636.97 and the DAX 2.2% to 25,337.27, led by chip-equipment makers. London's FTSE 250 rose 1.7% to 24,061.90, its biggest jump since April, with banks and miners leading. Gold rose nearly 4% to about $3,651 an ounce, while Brent crude fell 3.5% to $89.37 as a Libyan pipeline restarted and Middle East supply rose. The dollar hit a 19-month high as traders bet on Fed rate rises, so the pound slipped 0.4% to $1.3032. A flash PMI (an early business survey, where above 50 means growth) showed UK activity slowing slightly in November, to 52.3 from 52.9.

On Wednesday at 13:30 UK time the US publishes third-quarter GDP and October PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred inflation measure. US markets are shut on Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday. Severn Trent goes ex-dividend on Thursday 26 November and NextEra on Friday 27 November, with Nvidia following on 2 December. CME FedWatch puts the chance of a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December at about 96%, and traders now see about an 85% chance of a Bank of England rise on 17 December, up from about 80% last week. The ECB also meets on 17 December and is expected to raise rates.
Benchmarks: how to judge an investment against a fair yardstick, and why a portfolio's gap to a global tracker can swing sharply in a single day. Today's lesson goes through it, with a quiz.

brief.standfirst: The S&P 500 jumped 4.7% to 7,237.17 and the Nasdaq 6.5% to 24,089.56, as Nvidia soared 31.5%. The FTSE 100 rose 1.3% to 10,480.82, ending a five-day losing run.
